items.title: Instruction-tuning large language models with medical classification data improves ICD coding of German tumor diagnoses
items.abstract: Abstract Accurate coding of tumor diagnoses, with the German Modification of the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10-GM), and the International Classification of Diseases for Oncology, Third Edition (ICD-O-3), is essential for structured cancer documentation. Large language models (LLMs) offer opportunities for automating such tasks, but locally deployable, open-weight models often lack sufficient domain-specific coding expertise. This study investigates whether instruction-based fine-tuning on public classification resources improves the coding accuracy of open-weight LLMs for German tumor diagnosis texts. Eight models from the Qwen, Llama, and Mistral families (7–70 billion parameters) were fine-tuned on over 500,000 question-answer pairs based on the ICD-10-GM, ICD-O-3, and German procedure classification. The evaluation uses coded diagnoses from the local tumor documentation system as test data. ICD-10-GM accuracy rose from 1.4 to 24 to 41–58%, and partial (three-character codes only) accuracy from 31 to 74 to 73–83%. The accuracy of ICD-O-3 topography coding also improved but started and remained considerably lower. Malformed code outputs dropped to nearly 0% for almost all models. Tumor-diagnosis recognition reached 99%. A data quality analysis showed that incomplete diagnosis descriptions limited achievable test performance. Accuracy correlated positively with model size, but gaps between small and large models narrowed after fine-tuning. The reasoning mode in Qwen3 generally yielded lower performance than fine-tuning and was over 100 times slower. Our findings highlight the potential of leveraging public catalogues to build instruction datasets that improve LLMs in medical documentation tasks. To support reproducibility and further research, we publicly release the complete training dataset and the best-performing fine-tuned model checkpoints.

items.title: Integrating AI Interactional Competence Into Models of Communicative Competence: Human–Machine Collaborative Communication
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The advent of sophisticated LLMs and their integration into daily communicative practices represents a significant contextual development for the field of TEFL and Applied Linguistics. As a conceptual contribution, this paper argues that existing models of communicative competence, most notably Canale and Swain's foundational framework, require expansion to adequately describe the realities of language use in AI‐saturated environments. When learners employ AI for translation, drafting, and polishing, their communicative competence is no longer a purely human‐to‐human construct but can become a collaborative human–AI endeavor. This paper proposes an additional and context‐dependent dimension that complements traditional models: AI Interactional Competence (AIIC), which denotes the competencies required for direct human–AI collaboration and co‐construction of meaning. The paper deconstructs AIIC into three constituents: Prompt Crafting Literacy, AI Output Evaluation Literacy, and Ethical and Strategic Mediation Literacy. Drawing on the historical evolution of communicative competence models, digital literacies, human‐computer interaction, critical pedagogy, and posthumanist applied linguistics, this article provides a theoretical update for reshaping pedagogy, assessment, and research in the age of AI. It is acknowledged that this model is provisional and supplementary competence relevant primarily in AI‐integrated educational and communicative contexts and requires empirical validation across diverse sociocultural and educational contexts.

items.title: Integration of Human Factors Analysis and Classification System (HFACS) and Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) In Fleet Traffic Accident Risk Analysis At PT Semen Indonesia Logistik
items.abstract: Traffic accidents involving distribution fleets are a safety concern that can be influenced by human factors, environmental conditions, supervision, and organizational factors. This study aims to identify the factors contributing to traffic accidents and determine risk priorities as a basis for developing recommendations to improve fleet safety at PT Semen Indonesia Logistik. The methods used are the Human Factors Analysis and Classification System (HFACS) and Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA). HFACS is used to classify factors contributing to accidents, while FMEA is used to prioritize risks based on the Risk Priority Number (RPN). The integration of these methods enables the study not only to identify accident causation factors but also to determine which risks require the most immediate attention. The HFACS analysis shows that Adverse Mental States is the most dominant category, with 35 occurrences (18.92%), followed by Decision Errors with 33 occurrences (17.84%) and Perceptual Errors with 28 occurrences (15.14%). Meanwhile, the FMEA results indicate that driver fatigue has the highest RPN of 504, followed by failure to maintain a safe following distance with an RPN of 378 and failure to detect objects in blind spots with an RPN of 324. Based on these findings, the recommended improvements include implementing fatigue management, regulating working hours and rest periods, providing defensive driving training, increasing blind-spot awareness, and optimizing driving behavior monitoring. The integration of HFACS and FMEA can support the systematic identification of accident causation factors and the prioritization of risk control measures.

items.title: Intelligent automation and neural networks for enhanced energy efficiency in ESPs systems: Optimizing chemical injection in Nantu 31
items.abstract: Discontinuities in chemical injection and dosing in conventional artificial oil lift systems generate technical problems and significant energy losses, which can be mitigated through intelligent automation. This project began with the design and development of the first automated chemical injection and dosing system with closed-loop control that integrates an Artificial Neural Network with Backpropagation implemented in a Siemens S7-1200 PLC, remotely supervised via satellite SCADA through Baker Hughes’ Production Link Expert platform, using a producing well and the transient current signals of variable frequency drives as indirect sensors of fluid rheology. A predictive model was then trained using historical data from the Nantu 31 well, owned by Andes Petroleum Ecuador Ltd. and operated by Baker Hughes, to dynamically adjust dosing based on operational variables. The validation process was conducted through both simulation and 30 days of field testing, entailing a comparative analysis between the automated system and the manual method to ascertain advancements in efficiency, accuracy, and stability. The findings suggest that the Intelligent Chemical Injection and Dosing System may mitigate human error from 40% to 8% through the application of Artificial Neural Networks with a Backpropagation (BP) algorithm. Production demonstrated an increase from 755 barrels of oil per day (BOPD) to 765.8 BOPD. Furthermore, a cost reduction of USD 21,900 per annum was observed in multifunctional chemical additives, concomitant with a notable diminution in energy consumption from 6.47 kWh/BOPD to 6.20 kWh/BOPD.

items.title: Intelligent cerebrovascular intervention: a deep learning approach to multimodal image processing, hemodynamic modeling, and 3D printing
items.abstract: Cerebrovascular diseases, particularly intracranial aneurysms, represent a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide. The integration of deep learning with multimodal imaging, hemodynamic modeling, and 3D printing offers transformative potential for personalized neurosurgical planning. However, the field lacks a comprehensive synthesis of methodological approaches, validation frameworks, and clinical translation pathways. This research provides a comprehensive analysis of deep learning-based approaches for cerebrovascular image processing, hemodynamic modeling, and patient-specific 3D printing, with emphasis on multimodal integration, methodological innovations, and pathways to clinical implementation. Following PRISMA guidelines, we systematically searched PubMed, IEEE Xplore, Scopus, and Web of Science for peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2026. Studies were included if they employed deep learning for cerebrovascular image segmentation, multimodal fusion, hemodynamic prediction, or 3D printing applications. Quality assessment was performed using tailored instruments for each methodological domain. From 1,847 initial records, 127 studies met inclusion criteria. Key findings include: (1) 3D U-Net architectures with attention mechanisms achieve state-of-the-art segmentation performance (Dice coefficients: 0.85–0.92) for major cerebral vessels, though performance degrades significantly for vessels < 0.5 mm; (2) Multimodal fusion strategies have evolved from early/late fusion to hybrid architectures incorporating transformers and cross-attention mechanisms, improving fusion fidelity by 15–25% over unimodal approaches; (3) Reduced-order modeling combining Proper Orthogonal Decomposition with LSTM networks enables real-time hemodynamic prediction while preserving > 99% of flow energy with < 10 modes; (4) Biomechanical characterization reveals that silicone elastomers more closely match native vascular tissue (elastic modulus: 0.02–1.16 N/mm²) than current 3D-printed materials (0.85–1.02 N/mm²), though both fail to replicate nonlinear tissue behavior; (5) Explainable AI methods (Grad-CAM, SHAP, LIME) are increasingly employed but lack standardized validation protocols and clinical expert involvement in evaluation. Deep learning-based multimodal integration has demonstrated significant potential for advancing cerebrovascular surgical planning, but critical gaps remain in small vessel segmentation, biomechanical material fidelity, standardized validation frameworks, and prospective clinical validation. Future research should prioritize foundation model development, physics-informed neural networks, multi-material 3D printing with programmable properties, and human-centered explainability evaluation to enable clinical translation.

items.title: Intelligent Energy Systems
items.abstract: The rapid growth of distributed energy resources and renewable technologies has increased the need for intelligent management of modern power systems. Microgrids offer a reliable, flexible, and sustainable solution by integrating local generation, storage, and controllable loads. However, their planning and control are complex due to uncertainties in renewable generation, varying load demand, and dynamic conditions. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as an effective tool to address these challenges. Techniques such as machine learning, deep learning, and optimization enable accurate forecasting of energy demand, renewable output, and system behavior.AI also enhances real-time control through adaptive decision-making and efficient energy management. This improves reliability, reduces costs, and increases resilience to disturbances. Overall, AI integration enables efficient resource use, minimizes losses, and supports the transition to smart, sustainable, and decentralized power systems.

items.title: INTELLIGENT WEATHER PREDICTION SYSTEM USING MACHINE LEARNING AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
items.abstract: Weather prediction supports agriculture, trans-portation, travel planning, and public safety. This paper presents an Intelligent Weather Prediction System that combines machine learning techniques with an accessible application interface. The proposed workflow uses weather observations such as tempera-ture, humidity, atmospheric pressure, wind speed, cloud cover, and rainfall, depending on the data source. It includes data collection, preprocessing, exploratory analysis, feature prepara-tion, model training, evaluation, and presentation of predictions. Candidate models include regression methods for continuous weather variables, Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) for suitable classification, regression, or sequential forecasting tasks. The application may also provide AI-assisted weather question answering and concise weather-news summaries when these components are implemented and connected to reliable sources. The system is intended to make weather information easier to understand and use. Actual performance must be measured on the selected dataset; no accuracy result is claimed in this draft. The final paper should report the implemented models, dataset, evaluation results, and system screenshots.

items.title: Intercultural–AI Synergies for Supply Chain Resilience: A Bibliometric and Topic Modeling Review of Global Systems Research (2000–2025)
items.abstract: Supply chain resilience has become a critical capability for organizations operating in increasingly volatile global environments, where disruptions propagate rapidly across interconnected economic, technological, and cultural systems. Although artificial intelligence (AI) and intercultural competence are both recognized as strategic enablers of resilient supply chains, research examining their combined systemic impact remains fragmented. This study provides an integrated bibliometric and topic-modeling review of the literature addressing the intersection of intercultural competence, artificial intelligence, and supply chain resilience. Using bibliographic data retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus, we analyze scientific production, collaboration networks, conceptual clusters, and thematic trajectories through Biblioshiny and SciMAT. To capture emerging conceptual patterns, we apply LDA topic modeling, which identifies 35 latent topics subsequently organized into four higher-order macroclusters: Global Risk Systems, AI-Enabled Resilience and Predictive Systems, Human and Organizational Capabilities, and Supply Chain Resilience and Sustainable Global Operations. Results indicate a growing convergence between organizational capabilities, artificial intelligence technologies, and resilience-oriented supply chain research. While AI and resilience emerge as dominant empirical themes across the dataset, intercultural competence appears primarily as an emerging conceptual dimension associated with global coordination, cross-border collaboration, and technology adoption in multicultural environments. Accordingly, the present study interprets intercultural competence as a complementary organizational layer that may support the implementation and effectiveness of AI-enabled resilience strategies within global supply chains.

items.title: Interdisciplinary Approach to Safety-Ergonomic Parameters of Tractors During Agro-technical Operations
items.abstract: In Serbia, there is a large number of tractors in operation with a considerable age structure, without a cab or a protective frame. These facts contribute to a significant increase in the number of accidents with injured and fatal persons during exploitation and transport, primarily due to the lack of evident subjective: safety, ergonomic, comfort, and other parameters. Tractors, due to their construction and traction characteristics (high geometric and mass center of gravity, large dynamic wheel radii, large clearance, high engine power, large transmission load variations, agro-technical operations on variable configurations, with falls and ascents, etc.), are very unstable working machines despite relatively low movement speeds. In order to influence the reduction of the number of accidents, ergonomics investigates the "man-machine-environment" relationship, which studies anatomical, physiological, medical, social, legal and other areas that contribute to the reduction of accidents and occupational diseases, while increasing efficiency, reliability, safety, etc. Special attention should be paid to the balance of forces within the analysis of the required static and dynamic stability of the tractor when moving up and down the sloping surface of the working terrain, especially tractors without a cab or a protective frame. In addition to the general state of tractor safety, this paper presents a draft of a short analysis of tractor exploitation when performing work operations on ups and downs in agro-technical and transport conditions, as one of the main reasons for accidents with injured and fatal persons. Also, the basic ergonomic-ecological parameters that are necessary to achieve the necessary, safety, ecological, medical, social, legal and other parameters are presented.

items.title: Interpretable driver behavioral state monitoring using facial landmarks for human-autonomous vehicle interaction
items.abstract: Introduction Behavior-aware robotic systems require both accurate human state recognition and transparent machine intent to support trust and safe collaboration. This study presents an integrated framework for autonomous vehicles combining a real-time vehicle state visualization interface with a calibration-driven facial-based behavioral state recognition module. Methods A Polaris GEM e6 autonomous vehicle equipped with drive-by-wire control and LiDAR served as the testbed. A real-time Human-Machine Interface (HMI) built with ROS and Foxglove Studio visualized localization, object detection, and driving states. Concurrently, a vision-based behavioral monitoring system used an Intel RealSense L515 camera, MediaPipe, and OpenCV to extract facial landmarks. Individual calibration established neutral baselines for eye aspect ratio, mouth aspect ration, and head rotation angles. A real-time threshold-based finite-state model facilitated data collection across five behavioral states: neutral, closed eyes, out-of-safe-zone, yawning, and fast blinking. Classical classifiers (Support Vector Machine [SVM], Random Forest [RF]), and deep learning architectures (Convolutional Neural Networks, Recurrent Neural Networks) were trained on a controlled indoor dataset using stratified k-fold cross-validation (k = 10), and evaluated on a hold-out outdoor dataset. Results The HMI provided stable, real-time visualization of vehicle state and perception, while the facial monitoring system achieved a ∼ 98.5% face detection success rate. The online heuristic model identified behavioral states and enabled high-quality data collection, capturing features with strong Kruskal-Wallis significance from the neutral state for closed eyes (EAR, p < 0.001 ), yawning (MAR, p < 0.001 ), fast blinking (blink rate, p < 0.01 ), though out-of-safe-zone was non-significant (head rotation, p > 0.05 ). Stratified cross-validation accuracy and F1-scores reached ∼ 91% for SVM and RF. On the outdoor test data, SVM maintained its performance, whereas RF dropped to a ∼ 70% F1-score due to inter-session variability and feature ambiguity. Deep learning architectures achieved test F1-scores ( ∼ 80%), comparable to the heuristic baseline model ( ∼ 81%). SVM was the most stable and best performing classifier, isolating its confusion to the out-of-safe-zone and neutral states. Conclusion Combining transparent interface design with personalized calibration supports human-aware autonomy. The machine learning framework provided interpretable monitoring, while real-time visualization enhanced situational awareness, together contributing to behaviorally responsive and transparent human-robot interaction platforms.

items.title: Jailbreak Attacks and Defenses on Large Language Models: A Survey
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in content generation and knowledge-centric interaction and have been widely deployed in education, healthcare, communications, and finance. To mitigate unsafe outputs, contemporary LLM systems incorporate safety-alignment strategies and content-filtering mechanisms. However, jailbreak attacks exploit adversarial inputs or generation-control mechanisms to bypass safety constraints and elicit harmful content. With the growing prevalence of multi-turn dialogue and multimodal interaction, these attacks exhibit increased stealth and potential for scalable exploitation. Although prior studies have surveyed jailbreak attacks and defenses, evaluation criteria remain fragmented, hindering fair and reproducible comparisons, and comprehensive reviews under a consistent evaluation framework remain limited. To address these gaps, this paper presents a comprehensive survey of jailbreak attacks and defenses targeting LLMs, grounded in a structured literature collection, screening, and coding process. We first introduce the essential background of LLMs and formalize the jailbreak attack process. We then propose two complementary evaluation frameworks to assess the performance of attack and defense methods, respectively. Building on these frameworks, we construct a taxonomy for jailbreak attacks based on the primary execution interface and manipulated object, as well as a defense taxonomy based on the stage of intervention within the model life cycle. We further provide a comparative and evaluation-oriented synthesis of representative methods in terms of their technical characteristics, application settings, strengths, and limitations. Finally, we identify key open challenges and outline future research directions for improving the security of LLMs against jailbreak attacks.

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Contemporary conversation around artificial intelligence is caught between two incomplete extremes. At one end sits unstructured, transactional prompting, which frequently flattens an author's natural voice. At the other end sits corporate information-technology compliance, which treats artificial intelligence purely as passive software or enterprise risk to be audited. Neither approach addresses what happens when an independent thinker and advanced artificial intelligence systems work together as partners across sustained intellectual and artistic creation. JosieVerse Enterprise (JVE) establishes a third path. Founded by poet, researcher, and systems architect Josie O. Magee Bélanger, JVE is a creative, literary, and research enterprise anchored in the foundational field of MultiDimensional Cognition (MDC) and its innate parallel-processing construct, MultiDimensional Intelligence (MDI). Sitting beneath and powered by MDC are the two operational spheres of JVE's ten-domain architecture: 1. Creative Intelligence (CI): The artistic and structural sphere of JVE, comprising four domains: Dimensional Perspective Writing (DPW), Dimensional Perspective Systems (DPS), Creative Systems Architecture (CSA), and Dimensional Perspective AI (DPAi). 2. Dimensional Relational Intelligence (DRI): The relational and governance sphere of JVE, comprising six domains: Governance and Safety Architecture (GOV), H+AI Relational Architecture (HAI), Multi-Model Collaboration Architecture (MMCA), Dimensional Communication Systems (DCS), Dimensional Communication Engineering (DCE), and Nervous-System-Aware Design (NSAD). Together, these six domains define how people and AI collaborators communicate, pace complex work, maintain role boundaries, and preserve personal sovereignty across sustained collaboration. Unlike conceptual frameworks that begin and end as abstract theory, JosieVerse Enterprise is anchored in completed literary art, including the inaugural poetry duology Beneath the Gathered Shade: Poems of Lineage, Seasons, and Survival (Volume I) and The Forever Drifting Poem: And Other Works of Dimensional Poetic Art (Volume II). This Foundational Charter establishes priority of conception and public baseline definitions across the entire architecture, followed by ten adoptable principles for human+AI practice and a concise Quick-Reference Glossary for readers. items.title: Journalism Students' Awareness, Attitudes and Perceptions of Use of Artificial Intelligence Tools for News Writing
items.abstract: Abstract The global adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in journalism has increasingly, offering benefits such as enhanced efficiency, accuracy, and the ability to process large volumes of data swiftly. Despite these advantages, there is a gap in research regarding how journalism students, who represent the future of the industry, perceive the integration of AI in news writing. The focus of this study is to examine the level of awareness of AI tools among journalism students, identify the benefits and the perceived challenges that could be attached to its adoption in news writing. The study adopted a survey technique and sampled 324 students of the Federal Polytechnic, Nasarawa. The findings show that Journalism students are aware of the existence of AI tools that can be adopted for news writing and the perceived benefits are more useful in writing precision and other scientific reports. The finding underscores the benefits of AI tools in the advancement of writing styles among journalism students. However, ethical concerns, high cost and restrictive accessibility to some of the tools are parts of the barriers affecting the use of the tools. It therefore suggests that, journalism institutions should incorporate ethical use and guides into their curriculum in order prepare students for the future on the use of AI tools that are directly related to journalism practices Key Words: Awareness, Attitudes, Perceptions, Artificial Intelligence, News Writing

items.title: Jueces LLM: acuerdo, sesgos y validez de la evaluación / LLM judges: agreement, biases and validity of evaluation
items.abstract: Los modelos de lenguaje se usan para evaluar respuestas abiertas, y sus resultados suelen resumirse en una cifra de acuerdo con personas o en un puesto de clasificación. Este artículo sintetiza once fuentes primarias y separa tres cosas que esas cifras mezclan: la métrica de acuerdo (porcentaje de coincidencia, kappa de Cohen o correlación entre rankings) y la población sobre la que se calcula; los sesgos medidos (posición, longitud o verbosidad, estilo y autopreferencia) y su tamaño en cada montaje; y el protocolo (comparación por pares o puntuación absoluta, con o sin referencia, con o sin intercambio de posiciones). En MT-Bench, el acuerdo entre GPT-4 y expertos es del 85 % cuando se excluyen los empates y del 66 % cuando se incluyen; el acuerdo entre expertos baja de forma paralela. La consistencia ante el intercambio de posición varía entre el 23,8 % y el 65,0 % según el juez en un conjunto de pares casi equivalentes, y cae cuando la diferencia de calidad es pequeña. Preferir texto propio tampoco equivale a favoritismo: en tareas con clave, la preferencia propia de los modelos fuertes coincide mayoritariamente con la respuesta correcta. Ninguna de estas magnitudes se presenta como propiedad general del juez ni se compara en una escala común. Se propone un protocolo de validación local, sin validación experimental, que fija la decisión, la población, la referencia, los empates, los controles y la incertidumbre. No se presentan experimentos nuevos ni un metaanálisis. items.title: KnitTrans: Coordinated Trajectory Transfer for Effective and Efficient LLM Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: Trajectory transfer from rollout to training affects both learning quality and system efficiency in large language model reinforcement learning (RL). Enforcing batch-wide training requirements can delay the admission of completed trajectories, resulting in higher architectural staleness: the additional parameter-version gap from disaggregated pipelining relative to colocated execution. Beyond admission, misalignment between data access and training consumption causes redundant movement and unnecessary waiting when transferring large trajectory payloads. We present KnitTrans, a system that coordinates the rollout-to-training path through three designs. First, constraint-preserving mini-batch admission allows flexibility in early mini-batch composition, while checking that enough capacity remains to satisfy the remaining quotas. Second, on-demand trajectory data access matches storage units to consumer assignments and overlaps micro-batch data preparation with computation. Third, multimodal encoding deduplication supports reuse across a mini-batch while preserving gradient contributions from all backbone micro-batches. Experiments show up to 93% lower architectural staleness than with train-batch admission, narrowing the learning-quality gap between disaggregated execution and colocated execution. On multimodal workloads, KnitTrans reduces transfer latency by two orders of magnitude and achieves a speedup of up to 5.8 times in transfer plus training over the baseline.

items.title: Knowledge and attitudes of Egyptian medical students towards artificial intelligence application in medical practice: a multicenter cross‑sectional study
items.abstract: Abstract Background The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has significantly impacted various fields, including medicine. As AI integration in medicine expands, medical students and professionals need to develop a comprehensive understanding of its applications. This study aimed to explore the knowledge and attitude of undergraduate Egyptian medical students regarding artificial intelligence application in medical practice. Methods A national cross-sectional study was conducted during the spring semester of 2024/2025 among undergraduate medical students from seven Egyptian medical schools. Participants were recruited using convenience sampling. Data was collected via a validated structured web-based questionnaire distributed through social media to assess students’ demographics, knowledge, and attitudes toward AI applications in medical practice. Results This study included 1438 medical students with a mean age of 20.3 years (± 1.9 years). Overall, 55.3% demonstrated good knowledge and 66.8% showed a positive attitude toward AI applications in medical practice. Good knowledge was significantly higher among students in higher academic years (3rd year AOR = 1.88, P = 0.006; 4th year AOR = 2.02, P = 0.007; 5th year AOR = 1.86, P = 0.034) and among those reporting peers and mentors (AOR = 1.35, P = 0.017), scientific papers and books (AOR = 1.71, P < 0.001), training courses (AOR = 1.43, P = 0.004), and mass media (AOR = 1.32, P = 0.036) as their main sources of AI information. A positive attitude toward AI was significantly more common among male students (AOR = 1.50, P = 0.001), 4th-year students (AOR = 1.97, P = 0.014), and those willing to enroll in an AI course (AOR = 1.30, P = 0.039). YouTube was perceived as the most valuable social media source for AI-related information (90.4%), followed by Telegram (86.6%) and WhatsApp (65.2%). Conclusions Although the Egyptian medical students recognize the inevitability of AI and are willing to learn, they are currently navigating this transition without adequate institutional guidance. To bridge the gap, medical schools must formalize AI education to integrate technical literacy and ethical reasoning directly into the core curriculum.

items.title: Knowledge Engineering With Large Language Models: A Capability Assessment in Evaluating Ontology Property Restrictions
items.abstract: Advancements in large language models (LLMs) offer opportunities for automating challenging and time-intensive Knowledge Engineering (KE) tasks. Constructing an ontology is particularly complex when modeling logical axioms, especially among novice knowledge engineers and domain experts with limited KE training. Consequently, ontologies often contain modeling errors, undermining ontology-based applications and hindering subsequent KE tasks. Thus, it is important to investigate how LLMs can support KE tasks such as the evaluation of ontologies. However, systematically evaluating LLM performance remains challenging due to a lack of comprehensive, task-specific benchmarks needed for such LLM capability assessments. As a result, selecting the right LLM to support knowledge engineers is nontrivial. This study investigates how LLMs can support four concrete ontology evaluation subtasks: detection, classification, explanation, and possible correction of modeling issues, focusing on the use of existential, universal, and cardinality property restrictions. We construct a benchmark of student-built ontologies and assess the performance of four LLMs—GPT-4o, ClaudeSonnet, DeepSeekV3, and Llama3.3—on these KE subtasks. Additionally, we exemplify an annotation framework for qualitatively evaluating LLM outputs and analyse the capabilities of each model. Our findings reveal differences in model behavior and task-specific strengths, underscoring the importance of selecting an appropriate model for each KE task.

items.title: L'usage de l'intelligence artificielle dans la prévision financière et la qualité de la décision stratégique : rôle médiateur de la qualité perçue des prévisions dans les entreprises marocaines
items.abstract: Les entreprises intègrent progressivement des outils d’intelligence artificielle (IA) dans leurs activités de prévision financière, mais les travaux consacrés au contexte marocain portent surtout sur la performance prédictive des modèles et peu sur la manière dont la prévision est mobilisée dans la décision. Cette étude comble ce vide en examinant si l’usage de l’IA dans la prévision financière et la qualité des données sont associés à la qualité perçue des prévisions, et si celle-ci est associée à la qualité de la décision stratégique. Elle contribue à la littérature en spécifiant la qualité perçue des prévisions comme mécanisme statistique de transmission entre l’usage de l’IA et la décision. Le design est mixte imbriqué, à dominante quantitative : dix entretiens exploratoires apportent un cadrage contextuel, puis une enquête non probabiliste auprès de 250 professionnels de la finance et du pilotage d’entreprises marocaines est analysée par PLS-SEM. Les résultats indiquent des associations positives, de force modérée à faible : la qualité des données (β = 0,259) et, davantage, l’usage de l’IA (β = 0,364) sont associés à la qualité perçue des prévisions (R2 = 0,250), elle-même associée à la qualité décisionnelle (β = 0,334 ; R2 = 0,207). L’effet indirect de l’usage de l’IA sur la décision est significatif (β = 0,121), à côté d’un effet direct (β = 0,197), ce qui correspond à une médiation statistique partielle complémentaire. Les entretiens et la question ouverte soulignent la gouvernance des données, la supervision humaine et l’accompagnement des utilisateurs, sans que le modèle les teste. Le plan transversal, la mesure perceptuelle et la validation incomplète des items appellent à la prudence dans l’interprétation. As finance functions digitalize, firms increasingly integrate artificial intelligence (AI) tools into forecasting, yet research on Morocco has mainly examined the predictive performance of models and says little about how forecasts are used in decisions. This study addresses this gap by examining whether AI use in financial forecasting and data quality are associated with perceived forecast quality, and whether the latter is associated with strategic decision quality. It contributes by specifying perceived forecast quality as a statistical transmission mechanism between AI use and decision quality. The study adopts an embedded mixed-methods design with quantitative dominance: ten exploratory interviews provide contextual framing, followed by a non-probability survey of 250 finance and management-control professionals in Moroccan firms, analyzed with PLS-SEM. Results show positive associations of moderate to small magnitude: data quality (β = 0.259) and, to a greater extent, AI use (β = 0.364) are associated with perceived forecast quality (R2 = 0.250), which is in turn associated with decision quality (β = 0.334; R2 = 0.207). The indirect effect of AI use on decision quality is significant (β = 0.121; 95% CI [0.070, 0.183]) alongside a significant direct effect (β = 0.197), indicating complementary partial statistical mediation. Interviews and an open-ended question point to data governance, human oversight, and user support as enabling conditions, which the model does not test. The study thus shifts attention from algorithmic performance alone to the organizational appropriation of AI-assisted forecasting. The cross-sectional design, the perceptual measurement of forecast quality, and the incomplete validation of the items call for caution in interpreting the findings.

items.title: LapaFM: A Laparoscopic Foundation Model via Multi-Stage Continual Learning
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence-based analysis of intraoperative laparoscopic videos has the potential to improve surgical decision-making and precision. However, effective surgical assistance requires models that can generalize across diverse intraoperative tasks. Here we present LapaFM, a foundation model for laparoscopic surgery trained on more than 20,000 minutes of surgical videos using a multi-stage continual learning strategy that mitigates catastrophic forgetting and inter-task interference. LapaFM learns multimodal visual representations and supports multiple tasks, including smoke removal, surgical phase recognition, instrument and polyp segmentation, and lesion identification. The model was evaluated on 13 retrospective and two prospective cohorts collected from different imaging devices. LapaFM consistently outperformed task-specific models and existing foundation models across datasets, and also generalized to gastrointestinal endoscopy tasks, including polyp detection and classification. Notably, it recovered over 90% of smoke-obscured frames and achieved clinician-level or superior performance in lymph node metastasis prediction and prospective polyp classification.

items.title: Large language model‐enhanced deep reinforcement learning for voltage control in active distribution networks
items.abstract: Abstract As active distribution networks (ADNs) become increasingly saturated with intermittent renewable energy sources, maintaining voltage within safe operational limits has become a critical and complex task, requiring advanced control methods beyond traditional rule‐based approaches. This paper proposes a novel voltage control framework that integrates a large language model (LLM) with the soft actor‐critic (SAC) algorithm to enhance the performance of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) in ADNs. The core idea is to leverage the LLM as an external knowledge source during the early stage of training to generate highly interpretable and physically meaningful control action suggestions for key voltage regulation devices. A dynamic action fusion mechanism is designed to combine the LLM‐guided actions with SAC policy outputs. As training progresses, the influence of the LLM gradually diminishes, ultimately yielding a fully autonomous SAC policy. Tests on modified IEEE 33‐ and 123‐bus distribution systems show that the proposed method outperforms the standard SAC in terms of convergence efficiency, voltage deviation reduction and control stability. It effectively mitigates policy oscillations during the early exploration phase and significantly reduces the switching frequency of mechanical devices under the learned policy, thereby contributing to longer equipment service life and higher operational reliability.

items.title: Large Language Models in Clinical Decision Support: A Critical Review of Progress, Limitations, and the Path Toward Sustainable Healthcare
items.abstract: Large language models such as GPT-4, Med-PaLM 2, and BioMedLM are being increasingly applied to clinical decision support tasks including diagnostic reasoning, clinical documentation, medical question answering, and patient-facing health communication, with several studies reporting performance comparable to trained clinicians on structured benchmarks. However, the current pace of adoption has outrun the critical evaluation of whether these models are genuinely safe, equitable, and sustainable for deployment in real-world healthcare environments. This narrative review argues that the existing literature has focused disproportionately on benchmark performance while giving insufficient attention to the conditions required for these models to function as trustworthy long-term clinical tools. Drawing on published evidence across medical informatics, clinical artificial intelligence, and natural language processing, we synthesise model performance across four clinical task areas and examine documented limitations including factual hallucination, demographic bias, and poor generalisability outside controlled settings that are already present in current deployments. We further identify five structural sustainability challenges that obstruct responsible deployment at scale, and propose a corresponding five-pillar framework alongside a priority research agenda for closing the gaps this review identifies. This review contributes a critically grounded perspective to the growing discourse on artificial intelligence for sustainable healthcare, with direct relevance to Sustainable Development Goal 3 (Good Health and Well-Being) and Sustainable Development Goal 10 (Reduced Inequalities), and offers concrete guidance for developing clinical models that are safe, inclusive, and viable across diverse global health contexts.

items.title: Large language models poorly capture how word order shapes representations of sentence meaning in the human brain
items.abstract: Abstract Large language models based on the transformer architecture are now capable of producing human-like language. But do they encode and process linguistic meaning in a human-like way? Here, we address this question by analysing 7T fMRI data from 30 participants reading 108 sentences each. These sentences are carefully designed to disentangle sentence structure from word meaning, thereby testing whether transformer representations of sentence meaning resemble those formed by the brain. We found that while transformer models match brain representations better than models that completely ignore word order, all transformer models performed poorly overall. Further, transformers were significantly inferior to models explicitly designed to encode the structural relations between words. Our results provide insight into the nature of sentence representation in the brain, highlighting the critical role of sentence structure. They also cast doubt on the claim that transformers represent sentence meaning similarly to the human brain.

items.title: Large-Scale Study of GitHub Copilot Trajectories
items.abstract: AI coding agents are increasingly integrated into software development workflows. However, most coding agent studies rely on benchmarks similar to SWE-bench, which assume autonomous agents operating in a single trajectory. This assumption does not mirror real-world usage, where developers interactively collaborate with agents. We address this gap by studying human-in-the-loop agent trajectories in the wild, focusing on 7,581 Copilot-authored PRs with publicly accessible session data. We find that 58% of Copilot PRs have no human intervention, and that when developers do intervene, collaboration is brief (median of 2 Human-AI loops). items.title: Law and technology convergence: Artificial intelligence and blockchain regulation
items.abstract: In the modern world, where digital technology plays an important role in people’s lives, artificial intelligence (AI) and blockchain technologies have been the major catalysts of innovation and socio-economic development. However, this rapid evolution of technology has been causing challenges to well-established legal systems. This study examines the current issues of the legal regulation of AI and blockchain technologies within both national and international contexts. This paper explores the attempts of governments and international organisations to create flexible and adaptive legal regulations that keep pace with the rapid progress of technologies and at the same time protect human rights and privacy. Ethical dilemmas, responsibility mechanisms and the importance of clarity in AI decisions are given special attention. Moreover, the study analyses the legal consequences of smart contracts, decentralised autonomous organisations (DAOs) and the way data is processed by AI within blockchain environments. The research highlights the international tendency towards convergence of digital laws by comparing legal approaches in different regions such as the European Union, the United States, South Korea, Kazakhstan, and other countries. The study proposes a comparative accountability-oriented framework for AI and blockchain governance, focusing on legal certainty, data protection, human oversight, innovation support, and cross-border interoperability.

items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally reshaping the landscape of organizational leadership, with travel management systems (TMS) emerging as a critical arena for this transformation. This chapter examines how contemporary leaders can effectively drive AI-enabled change within corporate travel ecosystems. Drawing on established leadership theory, organizational change models, and emerging empirical evidence, it explores the strategic competencies required to navigate the convergence of AI and travel operations. The chapter addresses the ethical dimensions of algorithmic decision-making, workforce adaptation challenges, and the imperative for data governance. Case-based insights illuminate how visionary leadership accelerates TMS modernization. Findings suggest that successful AI integration demands not only technological acumen but also emotional intelligence, change management expertise, and a commitment to inclusive innovation. The chapter concludes with a forward-looking framework for AI-ready leadership in travel management contexts.

items.title: Learning alone: language models, overreliance, and the goals of education
items.abstract: Abstract The development and ubiquitous availability of large language model based systems (LLMs) poses a plurality of potentials and risks for education in schools and universities. In this paper, we provide an analysis and discussion of the overreliance concern as one specific risk: that students might fail to acquire important skills, or be inhibited in the acquisition of these skills, because they overly rely on LLMs. We use the distinction between local and global goals of education to guide our investigation. In our view, the harm of LLM overreliance is specifically that it severs the connection between local educational goals (e.g., successfully solving a specific kind of math problem) and global educational goals (e.g., acquiring general skills for mathematics). Based on this analysis, we sketch three possible responses to the overreliance concern: preserving both local and global goals while making minimal changes to educational practice (a conservative approach), changing global and local educational goals (a revisionary perspective), and preserving global educational goals while changing local goals (an in-between view). Since different types of responses have different benefits and weaknesses, we think that it is likely that an optimal response ultimately combines elements from all three types.

items.title: Learning from drops: AI-guided integration of liquid biopsy features in cancer studies
items.abstract: Cancer is a major global health issue with rising incidence and mortality. Early detection, tumor characterization, and disease surveillance are crucial for timely, effective treatment and ultimately reduce mortality. Liquid biopsy (LB) has emerged as a valuable detection tool, offering a non-invasive method to detect tumor-derived biomarkers in body fluids and demonstrating translational potential. To increase biomarker sensitivity, high-throughput sequencing platforms deliver massive volumes of data. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is pivotal to enabling large-scale, complex data integration. This contribution assesses the current state of integrative AI-based research in the LB field and provides methodological guidance. First, we conducted a PubMed search and found that the literature is sparse in studies integrating LB features, particularly by applying AI. When adopting this approach, defining study objectives is crucial to guide subsequent methodological decisions, including study design, patient selection criteria, sample size, the nature of the LB features, and the metadata to collect. Specifically, we propose strategies and tools for data preprocessing, including normalization and batch-effect correction, as well as for handling outliers and missing data. Furthermore, we recommend various Machine/Deep Learning approaches for feature selection techniques to ensure model robustness, and we highlight the importance of undergoing rigorous internal and external validation of the selected models. Assessing clinical utility and interpretability is often overlooked but fundamental for real-world implementation. In conclusion, we provide the LB scientific community with AI-based methodological guidance to bridge the two fields and enhance the integrative analysis of LB features.

items.title: Learning from Nature: A Biomimetic Network Framework for Occupational Health and Safety Research
items.abstract: Occupational health and safety research has long relied on two ways of understanding harm. One traces the chain of conditions behind an accident, and the other forecasts the outcome of an incident from large bodies of recorded cases. Both treat the factors surrounding an incident as inputs pointing toward a result. Neither was built to ask how the categories of risk in a whole body of records are organized in relation to one another, independent of any single outcome. This paper addresses that gap through biomimicry, taking the way living systems organize their interactions as a template for reading how risk is organized in safety data. Ecologists have long described how two distinct sets of entities connect through bipartite networks, and they have developed a compact set of measures for reading the structure of those networks, covering whether interactions concentrate in a shared core or separate into compartments, which categories are specialized and which dominate, and how a system responds when its parts are removed. Occupational safety data fit this biological template, because the categorical fields that safety agencies record pair naturally into the same two-set form. Transferring these ecological measures to safety records, this study sets out how the measures map onto safety questions and illustrates their use across construction, mining, manufacturing, and healthcare. A worked example then applies the full procedure to a public dataset of 158,396 healthcare injury records, building the bipartite matrices and reading their nestedness, modularity, specialization, and robustness against a null model, which shows that the approach runs end to end on real administrative data. The study presents this as a proposed framework and a demonstration of its feasibility rather than a validated method and argues that this nature-derived structural reading complements rather than replaces the causal and predictive traditions.

items.title: Legal Protection for Bank Employees in the Era of Digitalization: A Normative Legal Analysis of Indonesian Labor Law and OJK Regulations
items.abstract: The rapid digitalization of the banking sector has transformed work structures, performance evaluation systems, and employment relations. While regulatory frameworks primarily emphasize consumer protection and financial system stability, limited attention has been given to legal protection for bank employees affected by digital transformation. This study examines legal protection for bank workers in the era of banking digitalization by analyzing its alignment with Indonesian labor law, Financial Services Authority (OJK) regulations, Bank Indonesia’s payment system policy, and personal data protection principles. Using normative legal research with statutory, conceptual, and analytical approaches, this article analyzes secondary legal materials and scholarly literature related to algorithmic management, digital surveillance, electronic performance monitoring, and workplace data governance. The analysis identifies three central issues: the transformation of work roles and performance targets, intensified digital surveillance, and unequal access to digital competency development. The study indicates a regulatory gap between labor law provisions and sectoral financial regulations, particularly regarding algorithmic transparency, workplace privacy, employee data protection, and psychosocial protection. It concludes that legal protection must be expanded through adaptive regulatory harmonization, human review of system-based employment decisions, proportional limits on workplace surveillance, and stronger protection of employee personal data.

items.title: LEVERAGING ICT AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-ENHANCED SYSTEMS TO IMPROVE STUDENT ENGAGEMENT AND COGNITIVE OUTCOMES
items.abstract: This study examined the association between the use of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enhanced systems, student engagement and academic performance among tertiary students in Nigeria. A cross-sectional correlational survey design was adopted. Questionnaires were administered to 200 students of Kwara State College of Education, Ilorin, and 184 usable responses (92%) were analyzed alongside academic records obtained from institutional files. Data were collected with a 30-item, 4-point Likert questionnaire (Cronbach's α = 0.85) and analyzed with SPSS using descriptive statistics, an independent samples t-test, and regression-based mediation analysis. Students reported high behavioural (M = 3.34) and emotional (M = 3.24) engagement, and moderate-high cognitive engagement (M = 3.14). Students with higher weekly use of adaptive learning platforms, intelligent tutoring systems and educational chatbots had higher mean academic scores (72.4%) than low-usage peers (66.8%), t(182) = 3.58, p < .001, d = 0.61 (medium effect). Student engagement partially mediated the statistical relationship between ICT/AI use and academic performance. The most frequently reported barriers were infrastructure limitations (88.0%), digital literacy gaps (53.8%), and cognitive overload or offloading (38.0%). Because the data are cross-sectional and drawn from a single institution, the findings indicate associations rather than causal effects and should be generalized with caution. The study recommends investment in reliable power and affordable connectivity, capacity building for lecturers and students, pedagogically guided AI use, and context-appropriate low-bandwidth tools.

items.title: Lifelong Context Adaptation through Bidirectional Memory-Skill Learning
items.abstract: Lifelong LLM agents must learn from an expanding history of interactions while making each decision within a bounded context window. Memory makes past experience available, but the agent may still need to infer how to solve each new task from the retrieved records. Skills provide reusable procedures, yet may omit the task-specific facts needed to apply them. Because retrieved memory and skills shape the agent's behavior, they also influence the experience available for future learning. We introduce MemCryst, a framework for lifelong context adaptation through bidirectional learning of memory and skills with a frozen language model. Recurring episodes stored in memory support skill creation and revision, and the interactions guided by those skills supply new memory for subsequent learning. Facts retrieved from memory and learned skills jointly form the agent's context, while task outcomes adjust the future retrieval influence of the records actually served without rewriting their content. Across ten settings spanning embodied control, long-document reading, conversation, mathematics, and code, MemCryst leads seven reported comparisons. On ALFWorld, joint serving achieves 63.17% success, compared with 59.83% for memory-only and 50.50% for skill-only serving. Code is available at https://github.com/tianyi0216/Memcryst.git

items.title: Lipid nanoparticle platforms for p53-targeted cancer therapy
items.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have emerged as the most clinically validated nanocarrier platform in oncology, transitioning from liposomal chemotherapy to the cornerstone of mRNA-based therapeutics. This review critically examines the evolving LNP landscape with a deliberate focus on p53, the tumour suppressor directly mutated or functionally silenced via pathway dysregulation in over half of human cancers and a unifying therapeutic target across diverse tumour types. We analyse LNP platform design, physicochemical properties, and structure-activity relationships that govern encapsulation, stability, and release. A dedicated section synthesizes p53-directed nucleic acid strategies delivered by LNPs, including p53 mRNA for wild-type restoration, siRNA for mutant p53 silencing, miR-34a mimics engaging the p53 downstream axis, and CRISPR-Cas9 components for TP53 correction. The review evaluates passive and active targeting, stimuli-responsive release mechanisms responsive to tumour microenvironmental cues, and the integration of p53 nanotherapy with immune checkpoint blockade. Clinical translation is appraised through key 2020–2026 milestones, notably the KEYNOTE-942 trial of personalized neoantigen mRNA-4157, which clinically validates the mRNA-LNP platform in oncology, alongside emerging preclinical and early exploratory p53 mRNA-LNP programs in hepatocellular carcinoma, non-small cell lung cancer, and pancreatic cancer. Persistent challenges, including liver-dominant biodistribution, anti-PEG immunogenicity, manufacturing scalability, and regulatory complexity, are discussed alongside artificial intelligence-guided lipid discovery and biomimetic approaches. By reframing LNP development around p53 biology, this review highlights how tumour-suppressor restoration offers a mechanistically coherent strategy to enhance therapeutic index, reprogram the tumour immune microenvironment, and extend LNP clinical benefit beyond the liver compartment across diverse tumour types. The synthesis indicates that p53-focused LNP engineering represents a convergent opportunity to unify diverse cancer nanomedicine efforts under a single, biologically grounded therapeutic paradigm.

items.title: Low‐Field MRI for Knee Imaging: Current Insights and Evidence From a Systematic Review
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Low-field magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has regained interest for musculoskeletal imaging due to advances in magnet design, hardware optimization, and artificial intelligence (AI)-based reconstruction, offering improved accessibility, patient comfort, and sustainability. PURPOSE: This systematic review aimed to explore and summarize the current status of low-field MRI for knee investigations. STUDY TYPE: Systematic review on MEDLINE, Cinhal, EMBASE, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar databases. PROSPERO protocol (CRD42024544354). POPULATION: Approximately 3400 participants (8-89 years) encompassing healthy volunteers, community-based cohorts, and patients with diverse knee pathologies were evaluated. Few studies incorporate phantom experiments. FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: This review covered a range of very-low-field (< 0.1 T), conventional low-field (0.1-< 0.29 T), and upper-range low-field (> 0.3 T-0.55 T) with standard, extremity, open, and weight-bearing/standing systems. SE/FSE and GRE sequences, 3D GRE quantitative protocols, and AI-based were used. ASSESSMENT: Two reviewers independently extracted data on knee protocols, technical parameters, diagnostic performance, and reported advantages and limitations. STATISTICAL TESTS: Study quality was assessed using appropriate JBI critical appraisal tools. A narrative synthesis and descriptive analysis of the findings from the included studies are provided due to the heterogeneity of the intervention and outcome. RESULTS: From 3726 records, 31 were included. Low-field MRI demonstrated high diagnostic performance for meniscal and ligamentous injuries but lower sensitivity for early cartilage degeneration. Weight-bearing MRI provided distinct functional information but not direct equivalence to standard MRI. AI-enhanced reconstruction was evaluated in a limited number of single-center, vendor-specific studies and was associated with improved image quality and diagnostic confidence. Important limitations included lower signal-to-noise ratio, reduced spatial resolution, protocol heterogeneity, and limited pathology-validated evidence. DATA CONCLUSION: Low-field MRI may provide a clinically useful complementary option for selected knee meniscal and ligamentous indications. However, heterogeneous evidence, influenced by field strength, scanner design, sequences, and reference standards, limits claims of equivalence with high-field MRI, particularly for subtle cartilage lesions. Advances in hardware and AI have improved image quality and efficiency; however, evidence is limited and larger standardized multicenter studies are required. EVIDENCE LEVEL: 5. TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 5.

items.title: Luxury fashion brands’ AI-powered sustainability chatbot communication: how information qualities and brand luxury perception shape consumer trust and behavior
items.abstract: This study examines how sustainability communication in luxury retail shapes brand trust and behavioral intentions, focusing on consumers' post-exposure perceptions of information quality and provider type. Building on perceived objectivity and perceived persuasiveness, the study explores how consumers evaluate identical sustainability information attributed to either a human agent or an artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot, and how these perceptions influence brand trust, information acceptance intention, and purchase intention. A scenario-based experiment with 346 participants was conducted, and the data were analyzed using PLS-SEM. Perceived objectivity and perceived persuasiveness were positively associated with brand trust, which inturn mediated their relationships with information acceptance intention and purchase intention. The indirect effect of perceived objectivity was significant only under AI communication, suggesting that algorithmic provider cues may strengthen the trust-mediated role of objectivity, whereas perceived persuasiveness remained consistently associated with trust and behavioral intentions across provider types. Subgroup analyses further suggest a conditional pattern: among consumers with lower perceived brand luxury, the links between brand trust and behavioral intentions were stronger under AI communication, whereas no significant provider differences emerged among those with higher perceived brand luxury. As these results derivefrom split-sample multi-group comparisons rather than a formal interaction test, they should be regarded as subgroup-based evidence. These findings extend luxury branding research by showing how AI provider cues shape perceived information quality in sustainability communication and by highlighting the need to align provider strategy with consumers' perceptions of luxury brands.

items.title: Machine Learning for Solar Thermal Energy Optimization and Smart Control
items.abstract: This chapter presents a systematic examination of how Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning techniques are transforming the design, operation, diagnosis, and control of solar thermal energy systems, including flat-plate collectors, evacuated tube collectors, and concentrating solar power plants. Principal ML methodologies surveyed include Artificial Neural Networks, Support Vector Regression, Gradient Boosting, Long Short-Term Memory networks, Transformer architectures, Physics-Informed Neural Networks, and Deep Reinforcement Learning. Applications are reviewed across four domains data-driven surrogate models for thermal performance prediction, ML-based irradiance and thermal output forecasting, intelligent fault detection and predictive maintenance frameworks, and AI-driven control strategies shown to improve annual useful heat delivery by 8 to 15 percent. Research challenges including data scarcity, model interpretability, and cross-site generalization are identified, with future directions proposed in federated learning, physics-informed architectures, and explainable AI.

items.title: Maintaining BMI and Nutritional Intake Using AI: A Review of Challenges, Proposed Solution and Future Scope
items.abstract: Maintaining a balanced Body Mass Index (BMI) and proper nutritional intake is crucial for health and well-being. With advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI), health monitoring and personalized diet recommendations have become more efficient. This review paper explores the role of AI in BMI and nutrition management by analyzing existing AI-based applications and their effectiveness. A comprehensive literature review was conducted, examining AI-driven solutions for BMI monitoring and nutritional analysis. Existing projects and applications were compared based on accuracy, efficiency, and user experience. Findings indicate that AI-powered applications significantly enhance BMI tracking and personalized diet planning. Machine learning models such as neural networks and deep learning improve accuracy but face challenges related to data reliability and user engagement. AI has revolutionized BMI and nutritional tracking, but further advancements in data integration and personalized recommendations are needed. Future research should focus on improving AI-driven diet plans and integrating wearable technology for real-time monitoring.

items.title: Making blue carbon governable in China: standardisation, local experimentation and policy implications
items.abstract: China’s dual-carbon agenda has elevated blue carbon from a broad ecological aspiration to an actionable policy domain requiring accounting standards, measurement, reporting and verification (MRV), and institutional implementation pathways. This article examines how blue carbon policies are made operational in China, focusing on the institutional and technical devices through which marine carbon sinks are rendered calculable, verifiable and governable. Drawing on Jasanoff’s notion of sociotechnical imaginaries, it treats blue carbon not as a pre-given natural–technical object, but as a policy object iteratively defined, quantified, verified and recalibrated through policy narratives, standardisation, methodological rule-making and local experimentation. Methodologically, the study combines thematic analysis of national and coastal local policy documents, standards, accounting guidelines and regional methodologies with semi-structured interviews with 12 domain experts across policy, research and market-facing practice. Four findings emerge. First, blue carbon is constructed as a governable climate space, with standardisation functioning as metrological infrastructure. Second, implementation follows a two-wheel structure in which national policy direction and unified accounting grammars are made operable through local devices such as platforms, carbon-inclusion schemes, funds, insurance and judicial compensation. Third, market-facing implementation depends less on willingness to trade than on whether methodologies and MRV systems can institutionalise uncertainty into verifiable rules at bearable cost. Fourth, structural bottlenecks—cross-department coordination, uneven local capacity and unresolved risk allocation—shape credibility and scalability. The article contributes a mechanism-oriented account of how blue carbon moves from policy ambition to institutional operation under uncertainty.

items.title: MANAGEMENT MODEL FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE BASED ON EUROPEAN EXPERIENCE
items.abstract: The article focuses on the development of a management model for the implementation of artificial intelligence technologies in Ukrainian industry, aimed at ensuring a transition from an enterprise’s technological and organizational readiness to measurable performance outcomes from the use of artificial intelligence. The relevance of the study is determined by the need to accelerate the digital transformation of Ukraine’s industrial sector under conditions of limited financial and human resources, energy-related risks, changes in production chains, and the gradual integration of Ukrainian enterprises into the European digital environment. The study systematizes the key prerequisites that determine an enterprise’s capacity to use artificial intelligence technologies, including the state of technological infrastructure, data quality and accessibility, organizational conditions, staff competencies, economic capabilities, and interaction with the external digital environment. The necessity of distinguishing between the concepts of artificial intelligence readiness, artificial intelligence implementation, and artificial intelligence performance is substantiated. The proposed approach provides not only for the possibility of scaling a solution but also for returning to the stage of use-case selection to adjust the selected scenario or terminate the project in cases of insufficient performance. The practical significance of the obtained results lies in the possibility of applying the proposed management logic by managers and specialists of industrial enterprises when developing a portfolio of digital initiatives, selecting artificial intelligence projects, determining criteria for their piloting, and making decisions on scaling. Particular attention is paid to the European experience of using artificial intelligence in industry, particularly in energy, semiconductor manufacturing, automotive manufacturing, and industrial automation, which makes it possible to identify directions for adapting such experience to Ukrainian conditions. The study results in a management model that integrates enterprise readiness, practical technology implementation, assessment of the achieved effect, management decision-making, and subsequent performance into a unified cyclical process.
